proposal.title: A 1996 FBI Report Places the Mogilevich Organization in Budapest
proposal.description_short: A 1996 FBI report described the Mogilevich Organization as Budapest-based and linked it to the Ivankov organization.
proposal.description_medium: The FBI’s 1996 Eurasian organized-crime report described the Semion Mogilevich Organization as based in Budapest and tied it to the Vyacheslav Ivankov Organization. The Independent separately reported that Mogilevich moved his operations to Budapest in 1990. Seth Hettena’s later account quotes an FBI agent saying Ivankov was eventually found in a Trump Towers condo. These sources do not establish Donald Trump’s knowledge or involvement.
proposal.description_long: The FBI’s 1996 Eurasian organized-crime report described the Semion Mogilevich Organization as based in Budapest, Hungary, and identified ties to the Vyacheslav Ivankov Organization. That report supports the organization’s location and the reported network link at the time of the document; it does not, by itself, establish the date or circumstances of a move. In a 1999 article, The Independent reported that Mogilevich moved his operations to Budapest in 1990 after marrying a Hungarian woman. Separately, journalist Seth Hettena’s 2017 account quotes Robert I. Friedman’s book, including FBI agent James Moody’s recollection that investigators eventually found Ivankov in a luxury condo in Trump Towers; Hettena also says the phone book Friedman obtained included Trump Organization numbers. Together, the sources support only an attributed account of a Budapest-based Mogilevich organization and a separate reported Trump Tower connection through Ivankov. They do not show that Donald Trump knew Ivankov or Mogilevich, that Trump was involved in Mogilevich’s operations, or that the Budapest move was connected to Trump. The original allegations about stealing from emigrants, laundering with Robert Maxwell, and KGB ties are omitted because the sources mapped here do not substantiate them.

supports: The Semion Mogilevich Organization is described as based in Budapest, Hungary.
The report says it is tied to the Vyacheslav Ivankov Organization.
The Independent reported that Mogilevich moved operations to Budapest in 1990 after marrying a Hungarian woman.
Hettena quotes a passage from Robert I. Friedman’s book that attributes to FBI agent James Moody the account that investigators found Ivankov in a Trump Towers condo.
Hettena reports that Friedman obtained Ivankov’s phone book, which included Trump Organization contact numbers.

limitations: Sources do not establish Donald Trump’s knowledge or involvement.
The report does not alone date Mogilevich’s move; the 1990 date is separately attributed to The Independent.
Claims about theft from emigrants, Robert Maxwell, and KGB ties are omitted as unsupported by the mapped sources.
